newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND - Milan stocks seen rising further in 97.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND - Milan stocks seen rising further in 97.

text.p: Milan stocks are set for further rises next year, with the BCI index forecast to reach about 750 points, some 15 percent above current prices, according to a Reuters survey of the 1997 outlook for world stock markets.
The range of forecasts for the index collected from 10 analysts earlier this week was 710 to 780 points. The market reached an all-time high on May 20 this year of 674.1.
The following is a selection of quotes from analysts who took part:
MARCO RICCI, PORTFOLIO STRATEGIST AT SELLA ASSET MANAGEMENT

"The optimistic outlook for 1997 is based on interest rates coming down. Italy is looking at a new scenario characterised by interest rates which are halved in respect to past rates." He expected investors to shift from short term government debt to medium and long term debt and into the stock market, giving shares a sustained boost.
"1997 profits will not be positive for Italian companies, interest rates may fall but the index is unlikely to rise a lot."
